options.content:
Ceph guards against silent data corruption by **scrubbing**: re-reading stored data and checking it is still intact. A **regular** scrub compares the bookkeeping of every copy; a **deep** scrub reads all the data back and verifies checksums, which is the slow, disk-heavy part. Every slice of data (a **PG**) must get a regular scrub every 7 days and a deep scrub every 28 days on spice. At petabyte scale a deep cycle takes weeks, so this board answers three questions: what is scrubbing right now, which hosts are busy with it, and is the cycle keeping up.

**Now / PGs**: how many PGs the cluster flags as scrubbing. A PG is flagged from the moment it is queued, so these counts run ahead of the scrubs actually reading data.

**Hosts**: a host counts as scrubbing when one of its disks is leading a scrub that made progress in the last 5 minutes. The data being checked is spread across many hosts, so other hosts read for it too; the read-throughput panel shows that load.

**Work outstanding**: measured, not estimated. monk reads every PG's last-scrub timestamp on the mon hosts and reports, per pool, how much data is older than the target interval it reads from the cluster's own config. 100% coverage means nothing is overdue. Byte figures in this row are stored (logical) bytes and must not be compared with raw capacity without the per-pool expansion factor.

**What good looks like**: the status block reads *On track*, cycle coverage is 100.00%, and no PGs are overdue. Coverage is weighted by stored bytes, which exclude omap, so the PGs overdue count is the one that catches an index pool falling behind. Orange or yellow bands across the charts mark periods when scrubbing was deliberately paused, which is the usual explanation for a flat line.

panels.title: Deep scrub status

targets.expr:
(4 * (max(ceph_osd_flag_nodeep_scrub{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}) == 1))
or (vector(3) and (sum(max by (cluster, pool_id) (ceph_scrub_breach_pgs{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster", depth="deep"})) > 0))
or (vector(2) and (sum(max by (cluster, pool_id) (ceph_scrub_due_pgs{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster", depth="deep"})) > 0))
or (vector(1) and (sum(max by (cluster, pool_id) (ceph_scrub_overdue_pgs{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster", depth="deep"})) > 0))
or vector(0)

panels.description: Deep-scrub verdict, worst state first. Deep scrub paused: nodeep-scrub is set, so every other number on this dashboard is explained by that. Past warn deadline: a PG is older than interval x (1 + mon_warn_pg_not_deep_scrubbed_ratio), the age the mon raises PG_NOT_DEEP_SCRUBBED at, so this state cannot disagree with ceph health. Behind schedule: ceph's own published scrub target for a PG is already in the past, meaning the scheduler is losing ground. Clearing backlog: PGs sit past the target interval but ceph is still on schedule for every one of them. That last state is normal, not a problem: ceph randomizes eligibility past the interval and pushes a deferred target, so PGs legitimately age past it. Judging this panel on age past the interval alone reported Behind on a HEALTH_OK cluster whose worst PG was minutes late.

panels.title: Behind ceph's schedule (deep)
panels.description: PGs whose next deep scrub ceph itself scheduled for a time already past. Unlike PGs overdue, this reads zero on a healthy cluster: it is ceph's own target, not a wall-clock age against the interval. Nonzero and sustained means the scheduler cannot keep up, and ceph_scrub_due_max_seconds says by how much; minutes is normal jitter, hours is a stall. scrub_schedule names only the nearest of a PG's two targets, so a PG late at both depths lands under whichever ceph named; read Past warn deadline, which comes from the stamps, when the depth has to be exact.

panels.title: Past warn deadline (deep)
panels.description: PGs older than interval x (1 + mon_warn_pg_not_deep_scrubbed_ratio), the age at which the mon raises PG_NOT_DEEP_SCRUBBED. This is the number that means data verification has actually slipped and the one to escalate on. Anything nonzero here is also in ceph health detail.

panels.title: Hosts scrubbing (regular)

targets.expr: count(sum by (hostname) (rate({__name__=~"ceph_osd_scrub_sh_(repl|ec)_chunk_selected", project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left(hostname) ceph_osd_metadata{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}) > 0) or vector(0)

panels.description: Hosts with at least one OSD that selected a shallow-scrub chunk in the last 5 min.

panels.title: Hosts deep scrubbing

targets.expr: count(sum by (hostname) (rate({__name__=~"ceph_osd_scrub_dp_(repl|ec)_chunk_selected", project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left(hostname) ceph_osd_metadata{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}) > 0) or vector(0)

panels.description: Hosts with at least one OSD that selected a deep-scrub chunk in the last 5 min.

panels.title: PGs scrubbing (regular)
panels.description: PGs flagged scrubbing but not deep. Includes PGs still reserving replicas.

panels.title: PGs deep scrubbing
panels.description: PGs flagged scrubbing+deep. Includes PGs still reserving replicas.

panels.title: PGs waiting for reservations
panels.description: PGs flagged scrubbing+wait: the primary is queued for replica scrub reservations.

panels.title: Scrub flags
panels.description: Cluster osdmap flags. SET means that scrub level is paused cluster-wide.

panels.title: Scrub activity by host
panels.description: Per host, over time: idle, regular (shallow) scrubbing, deep scrubbing, or both. 5 min activity window.

targets.expr: 2 * (sum by (hostname) (rate({__name__=~"ceph_osd_scrub_dp_(repl|ec)_chunk_selected", project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left(hostname) ceph_osd_metadata{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}) > bool 0) + (sum by (hostname) (rate({__name__=~"ceph_osd_scrub_sh_(repl|ec)_chunk_selected", project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left(hostname) ceph_osd_metadata{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}) > bool 0)

panels.title: Hosts scrubbing now
panels.description: Instant snapshot of hosts that are primary for a running scrub. regular / deep count OSDs on the host that selected a chunk at that level in the last 5 min; read is all scrub reads on the host, replica shards included.

targets.expr: label_replace(count by (hostname) (sum by (ceph_daemon, hostname) (rate({__name__=~"ceph_osd_scrub_sh_(repl|ec)_chunk_selected", project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left(hostname) ceph_osd_metadata{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}) > 0) or 0 * count by (hostname) (sum by (ceph_daemon, hostname) (rate({__name__=~"ceph_osd_scrub_dp_(repl|ec)_chunk_selected", project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left(hostname) ceph_osd_metadata{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}) > 0), "hostname", "$1", "hostname", "spice-ceph-(.*)")

label_replace(count by (hostname) (sum by (ceph_daemon, hostname) (rate({__name__=~"ceph_osd_scrub_dp_(repl|ec)_chunk_selected", project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left(hostname) ceph_osd_metadata{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}) > 0) or 0 * count by (hostname) (sum by (ceph_daemon, hostname) (rate({__name__=~"ceph_osd_scrub_sh_(repl|ec)_chunk_selected", project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left(hostname) ceph_osd_metadata{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}) > 0), "hostname", "$1", "hostname", "spice-ceph-(.*)")

label_replace(sum by (hostname) ((rate(ceph_osd_scrub_replicated_read_bytes{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m]) + rate(ceph_osd_scrub_ec_read_bytes{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m])) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left(hostname) ceph_osd_metadata{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}) and on (hostname) (count by (hostname) (sum by (ceph_daemon, hostname) (rate({__name__=~"ceph_osd_scrub_sh_(repl|ec)_chunk_selected", project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left(hostname) ceph_osd_metadata{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}) > 0) or count by (hostname) (sum by (ceph_daemon, hostname) (rate({__name__=~"ceph_osd_scrub_dp_(repl|ec)_chunk_selected", project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left(hostname) ceph_osd_metadata{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}) > 0)), "hostname", "$1", "hostname", "spice-ceph-(.*)")

panels.title: PGs scrubbing: regular vs deep
panels.description: mgr PG state flags, summed over pools. Regular = scrubbing - deep.

panels.title: PGs scrubbing by pool

targets.expr: sum by (name) (ceph_pg_scrubbing{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"} * on (cluster, pool_id) group_left(name) ceph_pool_metadata{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"} > 0)

panels.description: Pool name joined from ceph_pool_metadata. Pools with no PG scrubbing are hidden.

panels.title: Scrub sessions per minute
panels.description: Cluster-wide, all OSDs. A session starts when the primary begins reserving replicas, passes reservation when it starts reading chunks, and ends completed or failed (aborted, preempted, or reservation denied). Started running far above completed means the backlog is growing.

panels.title: Deep cycle coverage

targets.expr: 1 - sum(max by (cluster, pool_id) (ceph_scrub_overdue_bytes{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster", depth="deep"})) / sum(max by (cluster, pool_id) (ceph_scrub_pool_bytes{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}))

panels.description: Share of stored bytes whose last deep scrub is inside the target interval, measured from every PG's last_deep_scrub_stamp rather than inferred from read counters. Both sides are stored (logical) bytes, deduped per (cluster, pool_id) because every monk instance reports the same cluster-wide data. Byte-weighted, and stat_sum.num_bytes excludes omap: an omap-only pool like the RGW bucket index can go entirely overdue without moving this number, so read it alongside PGs overdue rather than alone.

panels.title: Data overdue (deep)
panels.description: Bytes in PGs whose last deep scrub is older than the pool's target interval. Same caveat as the PG count: work outstanding, not a breach. Logical bytes, so never mix it with raw capacity metrics like ceph_osd_stat_bytes_used.

panels.title: PGs overdue (deep)
panels.description: PGs whose last deep scrub is older than the pool's target interval. This is workload outstanding, not lateness: ceph randomizes eligibility past the interval and pushes a deferred target's not_before, so a healthy cluster always carries some. Use Behind ceph's schedule and Past warn deadline for the verdict; use this one for how much work is queued up.

panels.title: Oldest deep scrub vs target

targets.expr: max((time() - max by (cluster, pool_id) (ceph_pg_last_deep_scrub_stamp{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"})) / max by (cluster, pool_id) (ceph_scrub_target_interval_seconds{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster", depth="deep"}))

panels.description: Age of the worst pool's oldest deep-scrub stamp, expressed against that pool's own target interval read from the cluster. 100% means a PG has just reached the interval; above that it is overdue. Stated as a ratio rather than days so the panel is correct on any cluster: spice targets 28 days and sietch 7, and a fixed threshold would be wrong on one of them.

panels.title: Overdue by pool (deep)

targets.expr: sum by (name) (max by (cluster, pool_id) (ceph_scrub_overdue_bytes{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster", depth="deep"}) * on (cluster, pool_id) group_left(name) ceph_pool_metadata{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"})

panels.description: Overdue stored bytes per pool, named by joining ceph_pool_metadata on (cluster, pool_id). monk emits a series per pool and depth even at zero, so a caught-up pool draws a flat zero line rather than dropping out.

panels.title: Cycle coverage trend

targets.expr: 1 - sum(max by (cluster, pool_id) (ceph_scrub_overdue_bytes{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster", depth="deep"})) / sum(max by (cluster, pool_id) (ceph_scrub_pool_bytes{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}))

1 - sum(max by (cluster, pool_id) (ceph_scrub_overdue_bytes{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster", depth="shallow"})) / sum(max by (cluster, pool_id) (ceph_scrub_pool_bytes{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}))

panels.description: Coverage over time for both scrub depths. Unlike the read-counter estimate this replaces, it needs no warm-up window: it is true from the first scrape.

panels.title: Scrub age vs target (deep)

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (max by (cluster, pool_id, le) (ceph_scrub_age_seconds_bucket{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster", depth="deep"})))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (max by (cluster, pool_id, le) (ceph_scrub_age_seconds_bucket{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster", depth="deep"})))

panels.description: Age of the median and 95th-percentile stored byte since its last deep scrub, against the interval read live from the cluster rather than a hardcoded assumption. The quantiles merge every pool, but the target is per pool, so both bounds are drawn: below the shortest target nothing is overdue, above the longest everything is, and between them the merged view cannot say which pool a byte belongs to. The two lines coincide while every pool shares an interval and separate the moment one is overridden; the overdue stats beside this panel stay authoritative either way. The histogram carries gauge semantics under a histogram type: never apply rate() or increase() to these series, and its _count counts bytes, not events. Buckets are deduped per le across instances, so snapshots taken a refresh apart can briefly invert two adjacent buckets; the engine clamps them monotonic, which nudges the quantile rather than failing the query.

panels.title: Backlog composition (deep)
panels.description: The three thresholds together, which is how to tell a backlog that is draining from one that is growing. Blue is workload outstanding and has a nonzero floor on a healthy cluster. Orange is the scheduler losing ground. Red is the policy miss the mon warns on. A scrub pause shows here as blue climbing while orange and red stay flat, then all of it draining once the flag clears; the pause annotations mark the window.

panels.title: Hosts actively scrubbing

targets.expr: count(sum by (hostname) (rate({__name__=~"ceph_osd_scrub_sh_(repl|ec)_chunk_selected", project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left(hostname) ceph_osd_metadata{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}) > 0) or vector(0)

count(sum by (hostname) (rate({__name__=~"ceph_osd_scrub_dp_(repl|ec)_chunk_selected", project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left(hostname) ceph_osd_metadata{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}) > 0) or vector(0)

panels.description: Hosts with at least one OSD selecting chunks at that level in the last 5 min.

panels.title: Scrub read throughput by host

targets.expr: sum by (hostname) ((rate(ceph_osd_scrub_replicated_read_bytes{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m]) + rate(ceph_osd_scrub_ec_read_bytes{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m])) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left(hostname) ceph_osd_metadata{project="yucca", cluster=~"$cluster"}) > 0

panels.description: Bytes read by scrubs per host, replica shards included: every OSD holding a shard of a PG under deep scrub reads it, so hosts that are primary for nothing still show load here. Shallow scrubs read metadata only. Stacked.

panels.title: Scrub reads vs physical disk reads
panels.description: Scrub read bytes from the OSD counters against physical device reads from node-exporter, plotted separately rather than stacked because they measure different layers: an OSD read served from page cache never reaches a disk, so scrub can and does exceed device reads (1.05x at peak over the last 30 days). dm-* and md* are excluded from the device series because LVM layers re-count reads already attributed to the sd and nvme devices beneath them. Client counters on the health dashboard are pool-level logical bytes and belong to neither series here.

panels.title: Scrub share of disk reads
panels.description: PGs whose next deep scrub ceph itself scheduled for a time already past. Unlike PGs overdue, this reads zero on a healthy cluster: it is ceph's own target, not a wall-clock age against the interval. Nonzero and sustained means the scheduler cannot keep up, and ceph_scrub_due_max_seconds says by how much; minutes is normal jitter, hours is a stall. scrub_schedule names only the nearest of a PG's two targets, so a PG late at both depths lands under whichever ceph named; read Past warn deadline, which comes from the stamps, when the depth has to be exact.
